Applying the vulnerability approach to the World Bank’s harmonized household surveys—estimating, for each economy, the probability that a household is living on less than the poverty line of the relevant income group over a few years, and identifying the consumption level at which this probability becomes low—yields economic security lines of about $6.00, $7.00, and $14.00 a day for the three income groups. This is roughly twice the corresponding poverty lines, but with wide variation across economies (Bolch et al. 2026). The threshold also shifts with the risks households face. In Europe and Central Asia, the income needed to maintain a low probability of falling into poverty rose by about 10 percent in real terms between 2008 and 2018 as the shocks pushing households into poverty grew larger (Bussolo et al. 2025). There is no fixed income at which security begins. The boundary of the

Global per capita income growth in low-income countries is projected to slow to its weakest pace since the COVID-19 pandemic, amid renewed energy-price shocks from the conflict in the Middle East (World Bank 2026c). Elsewhere, growth has remained stronger and more inclusive. South Asia, in particular, has shown strong, broad-based welfare gains across the distribution.4 Poverty is now concentrated in economies where progress has stopped Extreme poverty is highly concentrated geographically. More than half the extreme poor across the globe are concentrated in only 9 economies, and three-quarters are living in 20 economies (refer to figure 1.6).5 Of the nine economies, six are in Sub-Saharan Africa; the others are India, Pakistan, and the Republic of Y emen.

It is also a product of growth. As an economy’s average income rises, so does the share of the population that has attained economic security. The middle-income economies, home to about three-quarters of the world’s population (World Bank 2024b), are precisely the ones in which this transition is under way and far enough along that extreme poverty has receded, but not so far that security is the norm.

answer: Không. Kho tài liệu cho thấy không có mức thu nhập cố định nào đánh dấu điểm bắt đầu an toàn kinh tế. Theo cách tiếp cận dựa trên tính dễ tổn thương, các ngưỡng an toàn ước tính khoảng 6,00, 7,00 và 14,00 USD/ngày cho ba nhóm thu nhập, tức khoảng gấp đôi đường nghèo tương ứng, nhưng khác biệt rất lớn giữa các nền kinh tế [42d5e96ebee4eab749b0b04504c045356a3e531dac7bb893ecc6e12763370c22]. Ngưỡng này cũng thay đổi theo rủi ro: ở Châu Âu và Trung Á, thu nhập cần thiết để duy trì xác suất rơi vào nghèo thấp tăng khoảng 10% theo giá thực từ 2008 đến 2018 khi các cú sốc lớn hơn [42d5e96ebee4eab749b0b04504c045356a3e531dac7bb893ecc6e12763370c22]. Mức an toàn cũng phụ thuộc vào mức thu nhập bình quân của nền kinh tế: khi thu nhập trung bình tăng, tỷ lệ dân số đạt an toàn kinh tế cũng tăng [617f2d2ff4c85003af7ded4dfc15fad94224fd7f5e3f51562a574cb1b3c2c017].
